title: Conversion Spark — Ops Cooklet (first draft)
content:
One-line purpose: a compact, engineer-friendly quick reference for SEs to run pilot conversations that convert trials into reserved/dedicated commitments. Not a full deck — think: 1-page flip + speaker cues + triage checklist.

Audience: technical buyers (platform engineers, infra leads) and their SRE/ML infra partners. Use with ~5–12 minute live demos.

Core premise (1 sentence): show how Redwood reduces unpredictable token costs and latency risk during pilot and provide clear onramp to dedicated capacity when load and LTV justify it.

Quick flow (for a 12-minute meeting) — timed cues, speaker notes:
- 0:00–0:45: rapid context ("What system are you trying to accelerate / embed?") — ask: batch size, typical seq len, peak qps. Note: capture sequence-length distribution — this drives batching/quantization recs.
- 0:45–2:30: 30s value snapshot ("We route, cache, and quantize intelligently so average per-token cost drops without large latency regressions") + 45s example: customer X cut per-token cost 2.3x with prefix cache + micro-batching. (Speaker note: keep it concrete, avoid internal jargon.)
- 2:30–6:00: live demo / experiment quickshot — show a 2-call streamed gen on hosted API (short prompt vs long prompt) and toggle caching/pinning to show latency and cost delta.
  - Callouts: show token counts in console, explain fallback policy when dedicated capacity is recommended.
- 6:00–9:00: pilot success metrics and handoff checklist (see checklist below). Confirm which metrics buyer cares about (p50, p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 10k tokens).
- 9:00–12:00: rollout path and next steps (pilot -> reserved capacity -> private). End with 2 concrete asks: commit to 2-week pilot with X API keys + sample traffic, and agree on success criteria.

Top objections & short rebuttals (phrases for sellers):
- "We can't control cost spikes": "We set per-route cost windows + autoscale floor and an emergency fallback to cheaper quantized variant; we instrument token-level costs so you'll see exact bucketing in console."
- "Latency is unpredictable": "We provide p50/p95 by route and can pin traffic to a latency SLA (dedicated pools) while allowing overflow to a lower-cost pool."
- "We host everything on-prem": "We offer a private control plane and on-prem inference package; we can do a short security review milestone within the pilot scope."

Pilot success checklist (use as slide or shared doc during call):
- Signed pilot charter (scope + timebox) — include data sensitivity level.
- Sample traffic shape loaded into staging (seq len distribution + qps profile).
- Baseline run on hosted API (1–2 days) capturing p50/p95, cost per 10k tokens.
- One change experiment: enable prefix caching OR micro-batching OR a quantization variant and measure delta.
- Escalation/runbook: define if p95 > SLA persist then trigger canary to dedicated pool.
- Business metric: leading indicator (e.g., latency-linked CTR lift / throughput requirement).

Canonical pilot play variants (pick 1 for 2-week pilots):
- Latency-first: pin to small dedicated pool with burst backstop; measure p95 goal and error tail reduction.
- Cost-first: start hosted with KV prefix caching + 4-token lookahead batching; measure cost fall-through.
- Hybrid: dedicated for critical routes, hosted for low-criticality overflow; validate routing policy.

SE triage cheat (fast questions to map to play):
- Q: typical sequence length and variance? (if median < 256 -> favor quantization options)
- Q: steady qps vs spiky? (steady -> batching; spiky -> dedicated with autoscale config)
- Q: regulatory constraints? (if yes -> private pipeline)
- Q: acceptance criteria? (if tied to SLA -> latency-first play)

Slide order suggestion (compact 6 slides):
1) 60s problem + what we measure (p50/p95, cost per 10k tokens)
2) immediate demo/illustration (console view, showing tokens and latency)
3) pilot variants + recommended one for this account
4) success criteria + instrumentation points
5) escalation plan + fallback policies (model variants, routing)
6) ask + next steps (API keys, traffic sample, stakeholder list)

Metrics to capture during pilot (copyable table for the deck):
- route, p50(ms), p95(ms), avg tokens/request, total tokens/day, cost/day, error-rate(%)
(note: keep a CSV export template in shared pilot folder)

Ops-safe fallback script (for sellers to read out):
"If you see a sustained p95 breach, we do an automated shift to a reserved pool for the affected route and simultaneously spin up a quantized variant for non-critical traffic. Our console will surface the exact token cost change and notify both SE and the customer's SRE channel. We can rollback within 10 minutes if needed."

Language and tone notes for slides: avoid heavy infra jargon; use measurable outcomes and customer language ("latency", "cost", "SLA"). Keep slides visual: two micrographs (latency vs time, cost vs experiments).

Unresolved questions / TODOs (internal):
- Need a 1-slide visualization template (Priya) that shows both cost and latencies on same axis.
- Gather two short customer case snippets (Ethan) showing cost cut and latency improvement.
- Confirm default pilot contract length and credit amount for midmarket accounts (Finance ops).

Speaker-script snippets (copy-pasteable):
- Opening: "We typically see two levers that drive cost/latency: how many tokens you generate and how efficiently those tokens are produced. In a pilot we measure both, run one optimization, and show the delta within 2 weeks."
- Closing ask: "Let's spin up a 2-week pilot. We'll commit to baseline runs, one optimization experiment, and a joint review. If metrics look good, we'll scope dedicated capacity next."

Notes to self (workshop-style):
- Keep this doc <1 page when exported to slide notes.
- Don't overload with quantization math — surface the outcome and the risk tradeoffs.
- Add link to pilot CSV template in shared assets.

Quick links (internal assets):
- Pilot CSV template: https://drive.redwood/pilot-csvs/template.csv
- QA checklist for private deployments: https://confluence.redwood/private-deploy-qa

End of draft.
